agent_vs_you: The agent knew klein misspells, so it tried to dodge text: a demo screen 'with checkbox icons and abstract blue lines instead of written words', on klein with lettering off. That failed twice. klein still painted a garbled header ('DyVmning') and section labels ('Dsure Ensues'), as the catalogue warns it 'invents text'. And a to-do app whose tasks are blue strokes is not a credible demo, which is the judge's major fault. An app screen is a designed piece whose words carry the meaning, so I would make both demo states on qwen with lettering on and short real task names, quoted so the readback checks them. Because the catalogue says image-to-video 'CANNOT: readable text inside the motion', I would not morph lettered cards. I would show the change as a before/after inside one assemble: messy state, organised state (an image-edit of the messy one on qwen, so the style matches), then a designed ClearDay end card. The cut shows the transformation with every word exact. The agent also asked text-overlay for 'navy text on a white band'. The tool cannot do that (white text on a fixed translucent dark box), so it produced the dark-grey slab the judge called disconnected; a lettered end card avoids it.

your_plan.say: I'll design the ClearDay demo screen twice, first with a messy scatter of tasks and then with the same tasks organised into a calm daily timeline, and end on a blue-and-white ClearDay card, all silent in 8 seconds.

params.prompt_or_change: Flat, calm blue-and-white app UI mock-up on a pale blue background (#EAF3FF): a white phone-style panel with the header "ClearDay"; five white task cards with blue sans-serif text scattered at messy angles, overlapping on and around the panel: "Email Sam", "Groceries", "Gym", "Dentist", "Report draft". No other words.

steps.why: A credible UI needs real, readable labels. On qwen with lettering on, each quoted word is read back and fixed.

params.prompt_or_change: Same app, same blue-and-white style and background: the five task cards now sit neatly inside the white panel as a calm daily timeline with times, one per row: "8:00 Gym", "10:00 Report draft", "13:00 Email Sam", "15:00 Dentist", "18:00 Groceries"; the header "ClearDay" unchanged; nothing scattered outside the panel; no other words.

steps.why: An edit of the messy state keeps the same UI, so the two read as before and after of one app. qwen takes one picture and letters exactly.

params.prompt_or_change: Calm end card: pale blue background (#EAF3FF), the word "ClearDay" large in the centre in a clean rounded sans-serif, deep blue (#1D5FD1), a small simple sun-and-checkmark icon above it; no other words.

steps.why: A designed brand ending in the requested palette, replacing the pasted-on overlay band.

params.prompt_or_change: Messy, then organised, then the ClearDay end card; silent.

steps.why: Three pictures share 8 s (about 2.7 s each) with a gentle push-in, exactly 8 s at 16:9 and silent, with no generated motion to smear the text. 0 credits.

fix: (1) Planner rule: a UI, app screen, dashboard, menu or chart mock-up is DESIGNED LETTERING. It goes on qwen with lettering true and short real words, never klein with 'no words' (klein invents them anyway). (2) Catalogue line under image-to-video: 'a before/after of a lettered screen is two lettered pictures cut together in assemble, not a morph'. (3) text-overlay: honour the colour and band asked for in extra (color, box: none, band colour), or reject the instruction so the planner knows. Today 'navy text on a white band' silently became white on dark grey.
evidence: messy_tasks.png (640x360, klein) and organized_day.png (640x384, klein edit; the b2 harness did not crop edits) both show a white phone panel headed by a garbled 'DyVmning' with garbled section labels and blue strokes for tasks. The 1 fps grid of clearday_ad.mp4 (858x480, 8.0 s) shows the scattered cards gliding into a timeline, which is a real transformation, and the overlay 'ClearDay' in white on a dark-grey box over the bottom of the panel from 6 s. The judge's major fault (garbled headings, strokes instead of tasks) and minor fault (dark slab) are both visible, so the grader is right.
